summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and PEG dependence was admitted from a skilled nursing facility due to fever, dyspnea, and tachycardia. He was found to have septic shock and acute hypoxic respiratory failure secondary to multidrug-resistant organism pneumonia, with sputum cultures growing Proteus mirabilis and MDR Klebsiella pneumoniae. He required mechanical ventilation initially but was successfully weaned to trach collar support by day three and transferred to the medicine floor. Treatment included IV piperacillin-tazobactam and gentamicin for 14 days, guided by infectious disease. His kidney function remained stable, and he completed the course without complications. Oral vancomycin was continued for C. diff prophylaxis. Urinary retention was managed with finasteride, with plans to restart tamsulosin post-discharge. He was discharged back to extended care with PICC antibiotics and follow-up instructions.
problems: Pneumonia due to other Gram-negative bacteria
Acute and chronic respiratory failure with hypoxia
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with (acute) lower respiratory infection
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
